category: Shells, plates, membranes, beams, trusses, wires, pipes and the Composite Materials Module
description: Feature nodes of the Shell/Plate, Layered Shell, Membrane, Beam, Beam Cross Section, Truss, Wire and Pipe Mechanics interfaces, plus composite laminate modeling: ESL vs layerwise theories, laminate definition, laminate failure criteria (Tsai-Wu, Tsai-Hill, Hoffman, Hashin, Puck, LaRC03 and others), delamination, layered-material postprocessing and layered-shell couplings. Type strings were confirmed in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models where Java is shown.

tools.name: Thickness and Offset (Shell)
tools.description: Defines the thickness d0 of Shell, Plate and Membrane boundaries (default 0.01 m for shells, 0.1 mm for membranes) and an optional offset of the physical midsurface from the meshed boundary: Top surface on boundary, Midsurface on boundary, Bottom surface on boundary, or a user-defined relative offset z_rel (+1 means the bottom surface lies on the mesh). An expression gives a tapered structure; a Thickness Change subnode lets the thickness evolve (e.g. wear or corrosion).
tools.usage: Shell > Thickness and Offset (default node; more can be added). Java: physics("shell").feature("to1").set("d", "2[mm]"); set("OffsetDefinition", "NoOffset" | ...); set("z_offset_rel", "1").

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Shell thickness (constant or expression).

parameters.name: OffsetDefinition
parameters.description: NoOffset (midsurface), top/bottom surface on boundary, or user-defined relative offset.

parameters.name: z_offset_rel
parameters.description: Offset as ratio of half thickness.

tools.notes: Offsets are not available in the Plate interface and are ignored by Linear Elastic Material, Layered (the Layered Material Link provides thickness/offset). See existing entries Shell (shell) and Plate (plate).

tools.name: Linear Elastic Material, Layered (Shell)
tools.description: Shell material model for multilayer laminates using an equivalent single layer (first-order shear deformation) formulation; layer materials, orientations and thicknesses come from Layered Material, Layered Material Link or Layered Material Stack nodes. With the Composite Materials Module any number of layers is allowed; without it only single layers (still useful for nonlinear materials and multiphysics). Subnodes include Thermal Expansion, Damping, Viscoelasticity, Plasticity, Creep, Damage and Safety per layer.
tools.usage: Shell > Material Models > Linear Elastic Material, Layered (a sibling Hyperelastic Material, Layered also exists). Java: physics("shell").create("llem1", "LayeredElastic", 2); set("SolidModel", "Anisotropic" | "Orthotropic" | "Isotropic"); set("shelllist", "llmat1").

parameters.name: shelllist / allLayers
parameters.description: Layered material (link or stack) and layer selection; a single stack member can be picked for the multiple model method.

parameters.name: SolidModel
parameters.description: Material symmetry used in all layers (isotropic, orthotropic, anisotropic).

parameters.name: Transverse shear correction
parameters.description: Shear correction factors for the FSDT formulation (k13, k23 default 5/6).

tools.notes: Use the Layered Shell interface (layerwise) for thick laminates or when interlaminar stresses matter. Hyperelastic Material, Layered provides Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin, Ogden etc. for thin rubber shells (balloon_inflation_shell_membrane).

tools.name: Section Stiffness (Shell)
tools.description: Shell (and Beam) material model in which the homogenized section stiffness is entered directly instead of thickness and material: extensional A, bending-extensional B, bending D and transverse shear stiffness matrices (or the corresponding flexibility matrices), plus translational and rotational inertia. It is intended for corrugated, perforated, stiffened or sandwich panels whose properties come from a unit-cell homogenization; stresses can be recovered from user expressions of section forces.
tools.usage: Shell > Material Models > Section Stiffness (Beam > Section Stiffness for beams).

parameters.name: Specify
parameters.description: Effective stiffness (D_A, D_B, D_D, D_As) or Effective flexibility (D_a, D_b, D_d, D_as).

parameters.name: I0, I1, I2
parameters.description: Translational inertia (mass per area), rotational-translational and rotational inertia.

parameters.name: Stress expressions
parameters.description: Optional stress evaluation from computed section forces.

tools.example:
Shell > Section Stiffness 1 (corrugated sheet)
Specify: Effective stiffness, D_A, D_D from a unit-cell homogenization (Cell Periodicity study)
I0 = rho*t_eq
// Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Verification_Examples/corrugated_sheet
tools.notes: All data are interpreted in the local directions of the selected coordinate system. Supports Thermal Expansion, Initial Stress and Strain, External Stress and Damping subnodes.

tools.name: Pinned and No Rotation (Shell and Beam)
tools.description: Constraints specific to structural elements with rotational DOFs. Pinned fixes all translations but leaves rotations free (a hinge support at points, edges or boundaries); No Rotation fixes the rotations but leaves translations free (e.g. a sliding clamp). Together with Fixed Constraint and Prescribed Displacement/Rotation they give full control of shell, plate and beam supports.
tools.usage: Shell/Plate > Edges > More Constraints > Pinned | No Rotation; Beam > Points > Pinned | No Rotation; Truss and Wire > Points > Pinned. Java: physics("beam").create("pin1", "Pinned", 0).

parameters.name: Constraint Settings
parameters.description: Pointwise or weak constraints, constraint group for load cases.

tools.notes: In the Truss interface Pinned is the only point constraint needed because trusses have no rotations.

tools.name: Simply Supported (Shell)
tools.description: Edge condition for shells and plates that constrains the displacement normal to the shell and the rotation about the normal of the edge's in-plane perpendicular, i.e. the classical simple support used in plate theory benchmarks. The in-plane displacements along and/or perpendicular to the edge can optionally be constrained as well.
tools.usage: Shell/Plate > Edges > More Constraints > Simply Supported. Java: physics("shell").create("ssp1", "SimplySupported", 1); set("AlongEdge", "1"); set("PerpendicularEdge", "0").

parameters.name: AlongEdge
parameters.description: Also constrain in-plane translation along the edge.

parameters.name: PerpendicularEdge
parameters.description: Also constrain in-plane displacement perpendicular to the edge.

tools.notes: Available also on boundaries in the Plate interface. Use Symmetry/Antisymmetry for symmetry planes of shells.

tools.name: Shell Local System (Shell)
tools.description: Subnode of the Shell material that selects the in-plane local directions (1, 2, normal) used to interpret orthotropic/anisotropic data and to present local stresses and strains. A non-boundary coordinate system is projected onto the shell surface. The interface also creates a Shell Local System under Definitions that other physics and Coordinate System Surface plots can reference.
tools.usage: Shell > Linear Elastic Material > Shell Local System. Java: physics("shell").feature("emm1").feature("shls1").set("coordinateSystem", "sys1").

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Global, a boundary system or any user system (projected onto the surface).

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("shell").feature("emm1").feature("shls1").set("coordinateSystem", "sys1");
// plot shell.sl11 (local stress) with a Coordinate System Surface plot of the Shell Local System
tools.notes: Do not edit or duplicate the Shell Local System under Definitions; with several shell interfaces, reference only your own interface's system.

tools.name: Boundary to Boundary (Shell)
tools.description: Connects two parallel, geometrically disjoint shell boundaries (e.g. overlapping plates joined by glue, or midsurfaces offset from each other) point by point, either Rigid (virtual rigid bars to the nearest source point) or Flexible (spring constants per area, or properties of a joint material). Meshes do not have to match; the finer mesh should be the destination.
tools.usage: Shell > Connections > Boundary to Boundary.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Rigid or Flexible.

parameters.name: Connection properties
parameters.description: From material (E, nu, rho of the joint material) or user-defined spring constant per reference area k_u,A.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Global, Shell Local System or user system for the flexible stiffness.

tools.example:
Shell > Boundary to Boundary 1
Source: lower flange boundaries, Destination: upper flange boundaries (finer mesh)
Method: Flexible, Connection properties: From material (adhesive)
tools.notes: A Connected Region Indicator result template shows where the connection is active.

tools.name: Edge to Boundary and Edge to Edge (Shell)
tools.description: Mesh-independent connections between shell parts that do not share geometry: Edge to Boundary ties a shell edge to a shell surface (T-joints, slits from midsurface extraction), Edge to Edge ties two parallel disjoint edges. Each can be Rigid (with top/mid/bottom surface as connected location, accounting for thickness) or Flexible (springs from joint material or user data), and Edge to Edge can evaluate fillet or butt weld stresses with throat size and allowable stresses.
tools.usage: Shell > Connections > Edge to Boundary | Edge to Edge. Java (edge to edge): physics("shell").create("ee1", "EdgeToEdge", 1); set("connectionType", "Hard"); set("weldEvaluation", "1"); set("weldingType", "DoubleSidedFilletWeld"); set("throatWeldSize", "3[mm]").

parameters.name: connectionType / Method
parameters.description: Rigid (Hard) or flexible.

parameters.name: ConnectedSurfaceSrc / ConnectedSurfaceDst
parameters.description: Top, Mid or Bottom surface used on each side for rigid connections.

parameters.name: weldEvaluation, weldingType, throatWeldSize
parameters.description: Weld stress evaluation settings (Edge to Edge).

parameters.name: maxEqStress, maxPerpendicularStress
parameters.description: Allowable weld stresses for utilization.

tools.notes: Prefer Edge to Edge when edges match approximately; Edge to Boundary needs no matching edges.

tools.name: Spot Welds (Shell)
tools.description: Models any number of spot welds with common properties between two shell surfaces; weld locations are coordinate triplets independent of geometry and mesh. The elastic nugget connection (diameter, stiffness from a joint material or user values, including bending and torsion from the nugget area) is distributed over the nugget. Result templates tabulate normal and shear forces per weld and show nugget locations.
tools.usage: Shell > Connections > Spot Welds. Java: physics("shell").create("sw1", "SpotWelds", 2); set("Xp", ...); set("Yp", ...); set("Zp", ...); set("d_nug", "6[mm]").

parameters.name: Xp, Yp, Zp
parameters.description: Lists of weld coordinates.

parameters.name: d_nug
parameters.description: Nugget diameter.

parameters.name: nuggetStiffness / connectionProp
parameters.description: From joint material (Es, nus, rhos) or user-defined spring stiffness.

parameters.name: integrationOrder
parameters.description: Quadrature over the nugget area (automatic by default).

tools.notes: Delete and re-add the spot weld result templates if the number of welds changes.

tools.name: Interface Features and Shell Properties (Layered Shell)
tools.description: The Layered Shell interface distinguishes layer features (selected via the Shell Properties section: Use all layers or individual layers of a layup) from interface features acting on the surfaces between layers (Interface Selection: top, bottom, exterior, interior or selected interfaces). Interface versions exist for Fixed Constraint, Prescribed Displacement/Velocity/Acceleration, Roller, Spring Foundation, Thin Elastic Layer, Added Mass and Rigid Connector, e.g. to load or support only the top skin of a sandwich.
tools.usage: Layered Shell > Boundaries > Interfaces > Fixed Constraint, Interface | Prescribed Displacement, Interface | ... Java: physics("lshell").create("fixi1", "FixedIntS", 2); physics("lshell").create("dispi1", "DisplacementIntEP", 1); set("applyTo", "bottom").

parameters.name: allLayers / shelllist
parameters.description: Layered material and layers to act on (Shell Properties).

parameters.name: applyTo
parameters.description: Interface selection: top, bottom, exterior, interior, all or selected interfaces.

tools.notes: Requires the Composite Materials Module. Plain features (Fixed Constraint etc.) act on the layer material; the Interface variants act on layer interfaces.

tools.name: Delamination (Layered Shell)
tools.description: Interface feature that models failure of the bond between layers of a laminate using cohesive zone laws identical to contact Decohesion: displacement- or energy-based damage, linear/exponential/polynomial/multilinear traction-separation, mixed-mode Power law or Benzeggagh-Kenane criteria. The initial state can be Bonded or Delaminated; after separation it acts as contact between the delaminated layers.
tools.usage: Layered Shell > Interfaces > Delamination. Java: physics("lshell").create("del1", "Delamination", 2); set("InitialState", "Bonded" | "Delaminated"); set("CohesiveZoneModel", "DispDamage"); set("TractionSeparationLaw", "LinearSeparation"); set("FailureCriterion", "Power" | "BK").

parameters.name: applyTo
parameters.description: Interior interfaces (default) or selected interfaces.

parameters.name: StiffnessInput, kPerArea, ds
parameters.description: Adhesive stiffness: user defined or from material data and adhesive thickness.

parameters.name: sigmat, sigmas, Gct, Gcs
parameters.description: Interface strengths and critical energy release rates.

parameters.name: PenaltyFactor, pn
parameters.description: Contact penalty between delaminated layers.

tools.notes: Requires the Composite Materials Module. Mesh the thickness direction (layer elements) finely near expected delamination fronts.

tools.name: Continuity (Layered Shell)
tools.description: Connects two layered-shell boundaries that share an edge but have different layered materials (e.g. at ply drop-offs or thickness changes), enforcing continuity through the thickness on the common edge. Source and destination layups are chosen from Layered Material Links/Stacks, an offset on the destination defines the connected region, and a Layer Cross Section Preview shows the joint.
tools.usage: Layered Shell > Edges > Continuity. Java: physics("lshell").create("contls1", "ContinuityLayeredShell", 1); set("shelllist_src", "llmat1"); set("shelllist", "llmat2").

parameters.name: shelllist_src / shelllist
parameters.description: Source and destination layered materials (and selected layers in stacks).

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Destination offset defining the connection area.

tools.notes: The same node type exists in Heat Transfer in Shells and Electric Currents in Layered Shells.

tools.name: Wrinkling (Membrane)
tools.description: Subnode of Linear Elastic or Hyperelastic Material in the Membrane interface that activates a tension-field wrinkling model: membranes cannot carry compressive in-plane stress, so the stress is modified in wrinkled (one direction slack) or slack (both directions) regions. The node sets the Newton-Raphson tolerances of the local wrinkling equations (step size and/or residual, max 50 iterations).
tools.usage: Membrane > Linear Elastic Material (or Hyperelastic Material) > Wrinkling. Java: feature("lemm1").create("wr1", "Wrinkling", 2); set("termination", "steporresi"); set("maxit", "50").

parameters.name: termination
parameters.description: Step size, residual, or step size or residual.

parameters.name: maxit, abstol, reltol, restol
parameters.description: Local iteration limit and tolerances.

tools.notes: Theory: Wrinkling in the Membrane interface theory (tension field theory). Postprocess the wrinkling state variable to see taut/wrinkled/slack regions.

tools.name: Stabilization (Membrane)
tools.description: Adds temporary spring foundations to membranes during the first load steps, because a membrane without prestress has no out-of-plane stiffness and the problem is singular. With the Automatic method the springs are relaxed once stress stiffening is established; Manual lets you keep them for the first iteration, first step, a number of steps or while a Boolean condition holds.
tools.usage: Membrane > Boundaries > Stabilization. Java: physics("mbrn").create("stb1", "MembraneStabilization", 2); set("method", "automatic"); set("stiffnessMultiplier", "1").

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: automatic or manual.

parameters.name: activation
parameters.description: First iteration, first step, number of steps (nSteps) or user condition.

parameters.name: stiffnessMultiplier, iterationRelaxation, stepRelaxation
parameters.description: Scale and relaxation of the stabilizing springs.

tools.notes: Monitor the stabilization energy with a Global Variable Probe to ensure it vanishes before the final load.

tools.name: Cross-Section Data (Beam)
tools.description: Required Beam node defining section properties: Common sections (Rectangle, Box, Circular, Pipe, H-, U-, T-, C-profile, Hat) with their dimensions, User defined (area A, Iyy, Izz, torsional constant J, shear center offsets, stress evaluation points, warping), or data from a Beam Cross Section interface. In 3D a Section Orientation subnode fixes the principal axes.
tools.usage: Beam > Cross-Section Data > Section Orientation. Java: physics("beam").feature("csd1").set("SectionType", "RectangularSection" | "BoxSection" | "CircularSection" | "PipeSection" | "H_Profile" | "U_Profile" | "UserDefined"); profile dimensions hy_rect, hz_rect, do_pipe, di_pipe, hy_H...; user keys area, Izz, Iyy, J_beam, ey, ez.

parameters.name: SectionType
parameters.description: RectangularSection, BoxSection, CircularSection, PipeSection, H_Profile, U_Profile (T-, C-profile and Hat analogous) or UserDefined; values verified in Application Library models.

parameters.name: hy_rect/hz_rect, do_pipe/di_pipe, hy_H/hz_H/ty_H/tz_H, ...
parameters.description: Dimensions of the predefined profiles.

parameters.name: area, Iyy, Izz, J_beam, ey, ez
parameters.description: User-defined section properties and shear-center offsets.

parameters.name: BeamStressEvalMethod, yBeam, zBeam
parameters.description: Stress evaluation points in the section.

tools.notes: SectionType values were read from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models (the T-, C- and Hat identifiers follow the same pattern but were not seen). Truss uses the analogous CrossSectionTruss node where only the area matters (CircularSection, PipeSection, UserDefined).

tools.name: Section Orientation (Beam)
tools.description: Subnode of Cross-Section Data (3D) that orients the beam's local y axis either with a Reference point (the point and the beam axis span the local xy plane; default [1000,1000,1000] is fine only for symmetric sections) or an Orientation vector plus an optional rotation angle about the beam axis. Add several subnodes when the same section appears in different orientations.
tools.usage: Beam > Cross-Section Data > Section Orientation (also Pipe Mechanics > Pipe Cross Section). Java: feature("csd1").feature("so1").set("OrientationMethod", "vector_beam"); set("vector_beam", new String[]{"0", "1", "0"}); set("angle_beam", "0").

parameters.name: OrientationMethod
parameters.description: point_beam (reference point) or vector_beam (orientation vector).

parameters.name: point_beam / vector_beam, angle_beam
parameters.description: Reference point or vector defining local y, and rotation around the axis.

tools.notes: The reference point must not lie on the beam axis or its extension. Check orientation with a Line plot of beam.exl/eyl/ezl or the Beam dataset rendering.

tools.name: Beam End Release (Beam)
tools.description: Point node that decouples selected displacement or rotation DOFs between beams meeting at a joint, modeling hinges, sliding connections and semi-rigid joints (optionally with springs). With three or more beams at a point, Edge Group subnodes specify which beams stay connected. Directions follow the chosen coordinate system and rotate with the beam in nonlinear analysis.
tools.usage: Beam > Points > Beam End Release > Edge Group.

parameters.name: Release settings
parameters.description: Checkboxes for the displacement/rotation components to decouple.

parameters.name: Edge Group subnode
parameters.description: Groups of beam edges that remain connected to each other.

parameters.name: Edge defining the local orientation
parameters.description: Point evaluation (averaged) or a specific edge (Advanced).

tools.notes: Loads or constraints on a released DOF act on the average of the connected beams, which can be unintuitive.

tools.name: Homogeneous Cross Section (Beam Cross Section)
tools.description: Main node of the Beam Cross Section (bcs) interface: a 2D section geometry whose area, second moments, torsional constant, shear and warping properties are computed, and whose detailed stress distribution (including warping and shear from transverse loads) is evaluated for given section forces N, M1, M2, T1, T2, Mt and axial twist. Results can be passed to Beam or Pipe Mechanics via the Beam Cross Section-Beam coupling.
tools.usage: Beam Cross Section > Homogeneous Cross Section (default node; add Hole and Safety subnodes). Java: physics("bcs").feature("hcs1").set("N", "10[kN]"); set("M1", ...); set("Mt", ...).

parameters.name: E, nu
parameters.description: Material data (only nu affects the shear stress distribution).

parameters.name: N, M1, M2, T1, T2, Mt
parameters.description: Section forces for stress evaluation (Update Solution suffices after change).

parameters.name: Axial twist
parameters.description: Twist rate used for warping displacement.

tools.notes: Section properties are available as variables for use in a Beam interface's Cross-Section Data (From Beam Cross Section interface).

tools.name: Straight Edge Constraint (Truss)
tools.description: Truss elements have only axial stiffness, so internal nodes on an edge (more than one element or higher-order shape functions) would be singular in a linear analysis. The Straight Edge Constraint forces each edge to stay straight; Automatic adds it except for linear elements with one element per edge (the physics-controlled mesh default), On forces it, Off removes it.
tools.usage: Truss > Edges > Line Constraints > Straight Edge Constraint (default). Java: physics("truss").feature("sec1").set("constraintActivation", "automatic").

parameters.name: constraintActivation
parameters.description: automatic, on or off.

tools.notes: Not applicable to truss edges embedded in solids via Embedded Reinforcement. With geometric nonlinearity tensile trusses gain transverse stiffness.

tools.name: Spring-Damper Material (Truss)
tools.description: Truss material that turns an edge into a two-node spring and/or dashpot, a convenient way to add discrete suspension springs, dampers or cables between points of any structural model. Spring constant or force as a function of extension (truss.<tag>.dl), viscous damping coefficient and loss factor, free length or initial extension, and action Bidirectional, Tension only or Compression only; it can be deactivated (e.g. break) by a Boolean expression.
tools.usage: Truss > Edges > Spring-Damper Material. Java: physics("truss").create("spdm1", "SpringDamperMaterial", 1); set("SpringType", "kSpring"); set("k", "1e6[N/m]"); set("c", "100[N*s/m]"); set("SpringAction", "bidirectional").

parameters.name: SpringType, k / Fs
parameters.description: Spring constant or force as function of extension.

parameters.name: c, eta
parameters.description: Viscous damping coefficient and loss factor.

parameters.name: FreeLengthType, dl0 / lf
parameters.description: Initial extension or free length.

parameters.name: SpringAction, i_dac, PermanentlyDeactivate
parameters.description: Bidirectional/tension/compression only; deactivation condition.

tools.notes: Connect the truss points to solids/shells with shared points or Rigid Connectors. The global Spring-Damper node is an alternative without geometry edges.

tools.name: Elastic Wire (Wire)
tools.description: Material of the Wire interface for cables, ropes, guys and strings that carry only tension: axial stiffness kA and mass per length, with stiffness reduced exponentially under compression to beta*kA below the strain eps_c (slack cable behavior). The analysis is always geometrically nonlinear; sag under gravity, prestressed strings and guyed masts are typical.
tools.usage: Wire > Edges > Elastic Wire (subnodes Thermal Expansion, Hygroscopic Swelling, Initial Stress and Strain, Damping, Activation). Java: physics("wire").feature("elw1").set("k_A", "EA"); set("rho_L", "rhoL"); set("beta", "1e-4"); set("area", "A").

parameters.name: k_A
parameters.description: Axial stiffness (E*A).

parameters.name: rho_L
parameters.description: Mass per reference length.

parameters.name: beta, ecl
parameters.description: Compressive stiffness reduction factor and transition strain limit.

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: Cross-section area (for stress output only).

tools.notes: Give an initial stress/strain or small sag to avoid singularity of a straight unloaded wire.

tools.name: Pipe Cross Section (Pipe Mechanics)
tools.description: Section definition of the Pipe Mechanics interface: Circular (outer and inner diameter), Square, Rectangular or User defined pipe shapes, with optional wall-thickness reductions (inside/outside) used only in stress evaluation to represent corrosion allowances as required by piping codes. Section Orientation and Bend subnodes complete the definition.
tools.usage: Pipe Mechanics > Pipe Cross Section > Section Orientation / Bend. Java: physics("pipem").feature("pcs1").set("shape", "Round"); set("do_pipe", "di+2*t"); set("di_pipe", "di"); set("dt_o", "0[%]*pipem.t_nom").

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Round (circular), square, rectangular or user defined.

parameters.name: do_pipe, di_pipe
parameters.description: Outer and inner diameters.

parameters.name: dt_o, dt_i
parameters.description: Thickness reductions for stress evaluation (default 0 % of pipem.t_nom).

tools.notes: Stiffness uses nominal thickness; reduced thickness only affects stresses.

tools.name: Bend (Pipe Mechanics)
tools.description: Subnode of Pipe Cross Section for curved pipe segments (circular arcs): applies flexibility factors (in-plane, out-of-plane, torsion, axial) that reduce the stiffness due to ovalization, and stress intensification factors (SIFs) that raise the evaluated stresses, as prescribed by piping codes. Factors may depend on the bend characteristic pipem.hFlex; values below 1 are truncated.
tools.usage: Pipe Mechanics > Pipe Cross Section > Bend. Java: feature("pcs1").create("bend1", "BendCorrection", 1); set("kFi", "1.65/pipem.hFlex"); set("SIFi", "0.9/(pipem.hFlex)^(2/3)"); set("SIFo", "0.75/(pipem.hFlex)^(2/3)").

parameters.name: kFi, kFo, kFt, kFa
parameters.description: Flexibility factors for in-plane/out-of-plane bending, torsion and axial load.

parameters.name: SIFi, SIFo, SIFt, SIFa
parameters.description: Stress intensification factors.

tools.notes: The bend defines its own local system (y along curvature), overriding Section Orientation.

tools.name: Fluid and Pipe Materials (Pipe Mechanics)
tools.description: Main material node of Pipe Mechanics holding both the pipe wall's elastic properties and the density of the conveyed fluid (added mass), each taken from any Material node in the component (Edge material by default) or user defined. Subnodes add Thermal Expansion (including through-wall temperature difference), Initial Stress and Strain, External Stress, Safety and Damping.
tools.usage: Pipe Mechanics > Fluid and Pipe Materials. Java: physics("pipem").feature("fpm1").set("FluidMaterial", "mat2"); set("PipeMaterial", "mat1"); set("IsotropicOption", "Enu").

parameters.name: FluidMaterial, rhof
parameters.description: Material providing the fluid density, or user-defined density.

parameters.name: PipeMaterial, IsotropicOption, E, nu, rho
parameters.description: Pipe wall elastic properties and density.

tools.notes: Only one material can be assigned per edge, hence the separate fluid/pipe material lists.

tools.name: Fluid Load (Pipe Mechanics)
tools.description: Loads from the conveyed fluid on a pipe: internal pressure and external pressure (only the difference, i.e. gauge pressure, matters; absolute values when coupled to Pipe Flow), drag force per length along the pipe and centrifugal forces in bends. A default Fluid Load covers all edges; with the Pipe Flow interface the Fluid-Pipe Interaction coupling supplies these loads automatically.
tools.usage: Pipe Mechanics > Fluid Load. Java: physics("pipem").feature("fl1").set("p_in", "10[bar]"); set("p_out", "1[atm]"); set("fl", "0").

parameters.name: p_in, p_out
parameters.description: Internal and external pressure.

parameters.name: fl
parameters.description: Drag force per reference length (positive along edge direction).

parameters.name: fcf
parameters.description: Centrifugal force contribution in bends.

tools.notes: Show edge direction arrows in the View to check the sign of drag forces.

tools.name: Equivalent Single Layer vs Layerwise Theory (Composite Materials)
tools.description: The Composite Materials Module offers two laminate formulations. Equivalent single layer (ESL, Shell interface with Linear Elastic Material, Layered) is a first-order shear deformation theory: cheap and accurate for global response (deflection, buckling, eigenfrequencies) of thin to moderately thick laminates. Layerwise (LW, Layered Shell interface) uses full 3D displacements in an extra thickness dimension: accurate interlaminar and transverse shear stresses, delamination, nonlinear layers and thick laminates, at a higher DOF count.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Shell (ESL) or Layered Shell (LW); both read the same Layered Material Link/Stack. Mixed use: Layered Shell-Shell Connection (multiple model method).

parameters.name: Laminate aspect ratio
parameters.description: High (thin): ESL; low (thick) or when interlaminar stresses matter: LW.

parameters.name: Thickness discretization
parameters.description: LW: mesh elements per layer and shape order in the extra dimension.

tools.notes: LW for very thin laminates may show shear locking; ESL for very thick ones gives wrong transverse shear stresses. See also the existing Layered Shell (lshell) and Layered Material entries.

tools.name: Laminate Coordinate System and Ply Orientation (Composite Materials)
tools.description: The stacking sequence (ply angles in the Layered Material) is interpreted in a boundary coordinate system chosen in the Layered Material Link or Stack. Build it with a Boundary System whose first tangent comes from a global axis or another system (e.g. a cylindrical system with a manual axis for +-45 deg winding), and reverse the normal (globally or with Reverse Normal subnodes) to control the stacking direction. Result templates show fiber draping and a 3D view of the laminate.
tools.usage: Definitions > Coordinate Systems > Boundary System (Create first tangent direction from, Reverse normal direction); Materials > Layered Material Link > Coordinate system.

parameters.name: Create first tangent direction from
parameters.description: Global Cartesian axis, another coordinate system, or manual vector.

parameters.name: Reverse normal direction / Reverse Normal subnode
parameters.description: Flip the stacking direction on all or selected boundaries.

parameters.name: Ply rotation angles
parameters.description: Per-layer angle in the Layered Material, measured from the first tangent axis.

tools.notes: Check the orientation with the Layered Material fiber-direction result template before solving.

tools.name: Ply-Based Modeling and Variable Thickness Layers (Layered Material Stack)
tools.description: For laminates with many ply drop-offs the ply-based approach defines one Layered Material Stack whose plies each have their own boundary selection; COMSOL derives the zones and their layups automatically (Stack Zone Definition), instead of defining one layup per zone (zone-based approach). Layer thickness can vary with position through the Scale option of the Link or of individual stack members, e.g. tapered cores of sandwich panels; scaling also enables sensitivity/optimization with respect to thickness.
tools.usage: Materials > Layered Material Stack > Layered Material Link / Layered Material / Single Layer Material subnodes with individual selections and Scale expressions.

parameters.name: Ply selection
parameters.description: Boundary selection per ply (subset of the stack selection).

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Thickness scale factor expression (whole link or individual layer).

parameters.name: Stack Zone Definition
parameters.description: Automatically generated zones usable in physics and postprocessing.

tools.example:
Materials > Layered Material Stack 1 (all panel boundaries)
  Ply 1..6: Layered Material Link subnodes, plies 5-6 only on the reinforced region
  Core: scale = 1+x/0.5[m] (tapered core)
// Application Library: Composite_Materials_Module/Tutorials/ply_drop_off_in_a_composite_panel
tools.notes: Use Continuity (Layered Shell) where different layups meet at a common edge if they are defined in separate links.

tools.name: Micromechanics and Homogenization of Plies (Composite Materials)
tools.description: Multiscale workflow for composites: model a representative unit cell of fiber and matrix (Part Library micromechanics parts: unidirectional fibers, particulates, woven cells), apply Cell Periodicity in Solid Mechanics to run six unit load cases, extract the homogenized orthotropic/anisotropic elasticity (and thermal expansion) matrix, and write it to a new material used by the laminate (macromechanics) analysis.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Cell Periodicity (Automated Model Setup: create load groups and study, create material); Materials > Layered Material uses the created material.

parameters.name: Fiber volume fraction / cell geometry
parameters.description: From the micromechanics part parameters.

parameters.name: Computed properties
parameters.description: Elasticity matrix (standard or Voigt), CTE, density.

tools.notes: See the Cell Periodicity (Solid Mechanics) entry for settings.

tools.name: Tsai-Wu Orthotropic and Anisotropic (Safety)
tools.description: Interactive quadratic failure criterion for composite plies: the orthotropic form uses tensile, compressive and shear strengths in the principal material directions (optionally the plane-stress version), and the anisotropic form uses a second-rank tensor f and a fourth-rank tensor F in Voigt notation. It gives one failure index per layer but no failure mode.
tools.usage: Shell > Linear Elastic Material, Layered > Safety (Java type LayeredSafety) or Layered Shell / Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Safety; Failure Criterion = Tsai-Wu Orthotropic | Tsai-Wu Anisotropic. Java: set("FailureCriterion", "Tsai-Wu Orthotropic"); set("usePlaneStressVersion", "1"); material group OrthotropicStrengthParameters (sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass) or AnisotropicStrengthParameters (F_f, F_s).

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass
parameters.description: Tensile, compressive and shear strength vectors (3 components each).

parameters.name: F_s, F_f
parameters.description: Second and fourth rank strength tensors for the anisotropic form.

parameters.name: usePlaneStressVersion
parameters.description: Plane-stress formulation for thin laminates.

tools.notes: Several Safety nodes give combined failure index/safety factor/margin variables. Failure plots are placed in a Failure Indices group.

tools.name: Tsai-Hill, Azzi-Tsai-Hill and Modified Tsai-Hill (Safety)
tools.description: Quadratic orthotropic criteria derived from Hill's anisotropic yield function. Tsai-Hill (3D or plane stress) uses tensile or compressive strengths according to the stress sign; Azzi-Tsai-Hill (plane stress, ESL shells) and Modified Tsai-Hill (ESL) are common laminate-analysis variants. They are simple, interaction-type criteria without mode identification.
tools.usage: <layered material> > Safety > Failure Criterion = Tsai-Hill | Azzi-Tsai-Hill | Modified Tsai-Hill. Java: set("FailureCriterion", "Tsai-Hill" | "Azzi-Tsai-Hill").

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass
parameters.description: Tensile, compressive and shear strengths in principal directions.

parameters.name: usePlaneStressVersion
parameters.description: Plane-stress form (Tsai-Hill).

tools.notes: Azzi-Tsai-Hill, Norris and Modified Tsai-Hill are only in the ESL (Shell) formulation.

tools.name: Hoffman and Norris (Safety)
tools.description: Hoffman's criterion extends Hill's with linear terms, accounting for different tensile and compressive strengths in a single quadratic expression; Norris's criterion (plane stress, ESL) is a set of quadratic interaction conditions originally developed for wood and orthotropic plies. Both take tensile, compressive and shear strength vectors.
tools.usage: <layered material> > Safety > Failure Criterion = Hoffman | Norris. Java: set("FailureCriterion", "Hoffman" | "Norris").

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass
parameters.description: Strength vectors (OrthotropicStrengthParameters material group).

tools.notes: Hoffman is available in Solid Mechanics, Shell, Layered Shell and Membrane; Norris only for the plane-stress/ESL case.

tools.name: Jenkins, Waddoups and Zinoviev (Safety)
tools.description: Non-interactive, mode-separated orthotropic criteria: Jenkins is a maximum stress criterion (tensile, compressive and shear strengths per principal direction), Waddoups a maximum strain criterion (ultimate tensile, compressive and shear strains), and Zinoviev a maximum stress criterion with fiber/matrix mode separation (Composite Materials Module). They are easy to interpret and indicate which direction fails.
tools.usage: <material> > Safety > Failure Criterion = Jenkins | Waddoups | Zinoviev.

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass
parameters.description: Strengths for Jenkins and Zinoviev.

parameters.name: epsilonts, epsiloncs, gammass
parameters.description: Ultimate strains for Waddoups.

tools.example:
Layered Shell > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Safety 3
Failure Criterion: Waddoups, ultimate strains (1.2e-2, 0.5e-2, 0.5e-2) tensile, (1.0e-2, 2.0e-2, 2.0e-2) compressive
tools.notes: Jenkins and Waddoups are also available in Solid Mechanics for orthotropic solids.

tools.name: Hashin and Hashin-Rotem (Safety)
tools.description: Physically based composite failure criteria distinguishing failure modes: fiber tension, fiber compression, matrix tension and matrix compression (Hashin, 3D or plane stress) or fiber and matrix modes only (Hashin-Rotem). Separate failure indices per mode are available (fiber, matrix, interface variants), which makes them standard for progressive damage assessment of UD laminates.
tools.usage: <layered material> > Safety > Failure Criterion = Hashin | Hashin-Rotem (requires the Composite Materials Module). Java: set("FailureCriterion", "Hashin Orthotropic").

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass
parameters.description: Strength vectors in the principal directions.

parameters.name: usePlaneStressVersion
parameters.description: Plane-stress version of Hashin.

tools.notes: Labels in library models such as Fiber Failure Criterion / Matrix Failure Criterion come from separate Safety nodes per mode.

tools.name: Puck (Safety)
tools.description: Puck's action-plane criterion for UD plies: fiber failure uses ultimate longitudinal strains and fiber properties (fiber Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, mean stress magnification factor m_f of 1.3 for GFRP or 1.1 for CFRP), and inter-fiber failure evaluates stresses on the fracture plane with slopes p_tl and p_cl of the fracture envelope and a linear degradation stress. It predicts fracture mode and plane and is regarded as one of the most accurate ply criteria.
tools.usage: <layered material> > Safety > Failure Criterion = Puck (Composite Materials Module). Java: set("FailureCriterion", "Puck Orthotropic"); keys mf, ptl, pcl, epsilont1, epsilonc1, Ef1, nuf12, sigma1D.

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass
parameters.description: Ply strengths.

parameters.name: epsilont1, epsilonc1, Ef1, nuf12, mf
parameters.description: Fiber failure data.

parameters.name: sigma1D, ptl, pcl
parameters.description: Inter-fiber failure data (defaults 0.3 and 0.25 for GFRP; 0.35 and 0.3 suggested for CFRP).

tools.notes: Available in Solid Mechanics, Shell and Layered Shell with the Composite Materials Module.

tools.name: LaRC03 (Safety)
tools.description: NASA Langley LaRC03 criterion for UD laminates with separate matrix and fiber modes, in-situ transverse tensile and in-plane shear strengths (computed from ply strengths or given), and a numerical search for the fracture plane angle (alpha0 = 53 deg under uniaxial transverse compression, resolution 3 deg). It captures fiber kinking and matrix cracking under combined loads.
tools.usage: <layered material> > Safety > Failure Criterion = LaRC03 (Composite Materials Module). Java: set("FailureCriterion", "LaRC03 Orthotropic"); keys alphaF0, DalphaF, E1, E2, nu12, G12, epsilont1.

parameters.name: sigmats, sigmacs, sigmass, epsilont1
parameters.description: Strengths and ultimate longitudinal tensile strain.

parameters.name: In situ strengths
parameters.description: From transverse tensile / in-plane shear strength, from material or user defined.

parameters.name: alphaF0, DalphaF
parameters.description: Fracture plane angle and search resolution.

parameters.name: E1, E2, nu12, G12
parameters.description: Ply elastic data when the parent is anisotropic.

tools.notes: LaRC04 is not listed in the 6.4 Safety node; LaRC03 is the available LaRC variant.

tools.name: Layered Material Dataset
tools.description: Dataset that reconstructs a laminate modeled on a surface into a 3D solid of true or scaled thickness, so layered-shell and ESL-shell results can be plotted through the thickness. Evaluation can be on the full 3D body or on slices at mesh vertices, layer midplanes or interfaces; a thickness scale factor makes thin laminates visible.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Layered Material (created automatically by Layered Shell/Shell result templates). Java: model.result().dataset().create("lshl1", "LayeredMaterial"); dataset("lshl1").set("data", "dset1").

parameters.name: Scale factor
parameters.description: Thickness scaling for visualization.

parameters.name: Evaluate in
parameters.description: Full geometry or slices at mesh vertices, layer midplanes or interfaces.

parameters.name: Layered material / layers
parameters.description: Which layup and layers are shown.

tools.notes: Datasets in library models are tagged like dset1lshelllshl. See the Reference Manual for all settings.

tools.name: Layered Material Slice Plot
tools.description: Plot type that shows a quantity on selected layers or interfaces of a laminate as a set of in-plane slices, optionally arranged in a linear or rectangular array with automatic layer numbering, and at any relative position within a layer. Ideal for comparing ply stresses or failure indices of a [30/-45/75/-75/45/30] layup side by side.
tools.usage: Results > 3D Plot Group > Layered Material Slice. Java: model.result("pg1").create("lss1", "LayeredMaterialSlice"); feature("lss1").set("expr", "lshell.S11").

parameters.name: Layers / interfaces
parameters.description: Which layers or interfaces to slice.

parameters.name: Location in layer
parameters.description: Relative position within each layer (midplane by default).

parameters.name: Array layout, layer labels
parameters.description: Linear or rectangular arrangement and numbering.

tools.notes: Works for Layered Shell, Shell with layered materials and other layered interfaces (heat, electric currents).

tools.name: Through Thickness Plot
tools.description: 1D plot of any quantity versus the laminate thickness coordinate at selected geometric points, cut points or entered coordinates, e.g. the transverse shear stress distribution through a [0/90/0] laminate. The result is on the x axis and the thickness coordinate on the y axis.
tools.usage: Results > 1D Plot Group > Through Thickness. Java: model.result("pg2").create("thr1", "ThroughThickness"); feature("thr1").set("expr", "lshell.sl13").

parameters.name: Points
parameters.description: Geometric points, cut point datasets or coordinates on the reference surface.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: Quantity to plot, e.g. lshell.sl13, lshell.mises, failure index.

tools.notes: Combine with the Layered Material dataset for 3D visualization.

tools.name: Extra-Dimension Variables and Operators (Layered Shell)
tools.description: Layered interfaces define variables in the thickness (extra) dimension: <phys>.xd (0 at bottom to d at top), <phys>.xd_rel (0-1), <phys>.zl (-d/2 to d/2) and <phys>.num (layer number). Operators evaluate or integrate through the thickness: atxd1(xd, expr) and atxd0(xd, expr) evaluate at a thickness coordinate on layer or interface level, xdintopall(expr)/xdintopallint(expr) integrate through the thickness, and xdsumbnd(expr) sums over the thickness (e.g. total reaction forces).
tools.usage: In any expression field or result evaluation, e.g. lshell.atxd1(0.5*lshell.d, lshell.mises) or lshell.xdintopall(lshell.sl11).

parameters.name: <phys>.xd, xd_rel, zl, num
parameters.description: Thickness coordinates and layer number.

parameters.name: <phys>.atxd1 / atxd0
parameters.description: Evaluate at a thickness location (layer or interface quantities).

parameters.name: <phys>.xdintopall / xdintopallint / xdsumbnd
parameters.description: Through-thickness integration and summation.

tools.notes: The operators work with Solution datasets; the variables also work with the Layered Material dataset.

tools.name: Layered Shell-Structure Transition (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Connects the edge of a Layered Shell laminate to adjacent Solid Mechanics domains or Shell boundaries (e.g. a composite skin ending in a metallic fitting) with automatic detection of the shared region and a small connection tolerance (0.5 % of the thickness). The coupling can be restricted to selected layers.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Layered Shell-Structure Transition (Structure = Solid Mechanics or Shell). Java: multiphysics().create("lsst1", "LayeredShellStructTransition", 1).

parameters.name: Structure
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics or Shell.

parameters.name: allLayers / layer selection
parameters.description: Apply the transition to all or some layers.

parameters.name: connectionTolerance, tol
parameters.description: Automatic (0.5 % thickness) or user-defined extension distance.

tools.notes: Requires the Composite Materials Module.

tools.name: Layered Shell-Structure Cladding (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Bonds the top or bottom surface of a Layered Shell to the surface of a Solid Mechanics domain, Shell or Membrane, either on shared boundaries or on parallel boundaries (with a selected Shell top/bottom side), representing coatings, patches, liners or laminate overwraps on a structure.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Layered Shell-Structure Cladding. Java: multiphysics().create("lssc1", "LayeredShellStructCladding", -1); set("connectionSettings", "sharedBnd"); set("LayeredShellBnd", "Top" | "Bottom").

parameters.name: connectionSettings
parameters.description: sharedBnd (shared boundaries) or parallel boundaries.

parameters.name: LayeredShellBnd, ShellBndShared/ShellBndParallel
parameters.description: Which laminate and shell surfaces are bonded.

parameters.name: connectionTolerance
parameters.description: Automatic or user-defined tolerance.

tools.notes: Requires the Composite Materials Module.

tools.name: Layered Shell-Shell Connection (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Multiple model method: the Layered Shell (layerwise) and Shell (ESL) interfaces act on the same boundary but on different layers of one layup, bonded at their shared interfaces. Thick layers (e.g. a core) get layerwise accuracy while thin skins use the cheaper ESL formulation.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Layered Shell-Shell Connection (Apply to: Interior interfaces or Selected interfaces). Java: multiphysics().create("lssh1", "LayeredShellShellConnection", 2); set("applyTo", "interior").

parameters.name: applyTo
parameters.description: interior (all shared interfaces) or selected interfaces.

parameters.name: LShell_physics, Shell_physics
parameters.description: Coupled interfaces.

tools.notes: In the Shell interface select a single stack member in Linear Elastic Material, Layered so each interface covers its own layers.
